quotes.quote: Africa: widely distributed along eastern-draining rivers of Madagascar.

sections.html:
• Common name: Vaona
  • Dorsal spines: 2; dorsal soft rays: 6-7; anal spines: 0; anal soft rays: 14-15; vertebrae: 44-46.

Africa: widely distributed along eastern-draining rivers of Madagascar. Type locality: Tohizona, Madagascar. Ancharius fuscus has by far the widest range of any member of the family, extending from the region of Maroansetra in the north to the southeastern highlands; all other Anchariidae are known from only a single basin.
Ancharius fuscus is restricted to the middle to upper reaches of several river basins of the eastern coast of Madagascar and to habitats that are not highly degraded.

Diagnosis: Ancharius fuscus is distinguished from other Anchariidae by a shorter snout (40.1-45.8% of head length vs. 47.1-54.3), longer maxillary barbels reaching to the midpoint of the pectoral-fin base, a pectoral spine serrated along its entire posterior margin, and purplish-gray colouration. It differs from Ancharius griseus in having a shorter dorsal-fin spine (14.6-22.6% of standard length vs. 22.9-24.3%) and a larger eye (11.4-15.4% of head length vs. 9.3-10.1%).

Etymology: the genus name Ancharius comes from the Greek ánchi, near, referring to its similarity to Arius (Ariidae). The specific name fuscus is Latin for dark or dusky.

IUCN: population sizes and status are poorly known and this is not a common species anywhere in its range. Previously assessed as Data deficient, it is suggested to be reassessed as Least Concern, as the extent of occurrence is estimated at 63,000 km² and there is no sign of significant population decline.
